security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG does not decode Zisb instructions (TEB/MDB/DPB) as valid, causing illegal instruction traps for guest software that relies on them; OR QEMU KVM fails to advertise the Zisb extension to the guest when host hardware supports it, preventing guest kernels from placing speculation barriers at software-defined security boundaries
security_spec.summary: Zisb barriers (TEB/MDB/DPB) use Zimop MOP encodings; QEMU TCG inherently satisfies barrier semantics since it performs no speculative execution, but failure to decode these instructions as valid NOPs causes guest DoS via spurious illegal instruction traps; on KVM, failure to expose the extension to guests deprives them of speculation barriers needed for in-domain Spectre-variant mitigations on real hardware

findings.finding: Zisb extension completely unimplemented: no ext_zisb BOOL_FIELD exists in cpu_cfg_fields.h.inc. The TEB/MDB/DPB speculation-barrier instructions that use the MOP encoding space are not decodable by TCG, and the extension is not advertiseable to KVM guests. Guest software that emits Zisb barriers at security boundaries will receive illegal-instruction traps (TCG) or cannot discover the feature (KVM), causing denial of service.
findings.snippet:
BOOL_FIELD(ext_zimop)
BOOL_FIELD(ext_zcmop)
...
/* No ext_zisb field anywhere in this file */

findings.finding: The MOP decode space defines only NOP-like encodings (mop_r_n, mop_rr_n) that write zero to rd. No Zisb barrier instructions (TEB: MOP.R 0/1, MDB: MOP.R 2, DPB: MOP.R 3) are decoded. The mop_r_n pattern (1.00..0111..) may also mis-decode Zisb-occupied encodings as generic MOP NOPs rather than recognizing them as speculation barriers with distinct semantics.

MOP NOP translation treats all matched MOP encodings as register-zeroing NOPs. If Zisb barrier encodings happen to match the mop_r_n/mop_rr_n wildcard patterns, they would be silently executed as NOPs rather than triggering speculation barriers. This means guest software relying on TEB/MDB/DPB for Spectre mitigation would have ineffective barriers (silent failure, not illegal instruction).

No KVM_EXT_CFG entry for 'zisb' exists in the KVM extension advertising array. Even if the host kernel supports Zisb (KVM_RISCV_ISA_EXT_ZISB), QEMU cannot advertise or forward this extension to the guest, preventing guest kernels from discovering and using speculation barriers at software-defined security boundaries.

The KVM header defines KVM_RISCV_ISA_EXT_ZIMOP (line 175) but no KVM_RISCV_ISA_EXT_ZISB. This means either the kernel hasn't defined this extension ID yet, or the header is stale. In either case, QEMU cannot use a nonexistent constant to bridge host Zisb support to the guest.

No ISA_EXT_DATA_ENTRY for zisb exists in the ISA extension table, no MULTI_EXT_CFG_BOOL property registration, and no profile (rvb, rva22, rva23) enables ext_zisb. The extension is completely invisible to QEMU's CPU model system—it cannot be enabled via -cpu rv64,zisb=true and is absent from all profile/machine-type defaults.
